claims.text: The starting material is AlCrFeNiSi powder feedstock intended for laser powder bed fusion.
The proposed intervention is to preheat both the build chamber and substrate immediately before and during printing.
The proposed preheating window is approximately 300–350°C.
The intervention is expected to apply to laser-powder-bed-fused miniature components with millimeter-scale features.
Preheating decreases the temperature differential between the melt pool and the surrounding material.
The decreased temperature differential reduces thermal gradients across the build.
Reduced thermal gradients reduce rapid cooling.
Reduced thermal gradients produce a more uniform microstructure.
Reduced thermal gradients produce a lower dislocation density.
Slower, more controlled solidification produces a refined and homogeneous microstructure.
Preheating reduces residual thermal stresses relative to room-temperature laser powder bed fusion.
Preheating improves tensile properties relative to room-temperature processing.
Preheating improves fatigue properties relative to room-temperature processing.
Preheating reduces the need for post-processing treatments.
The intervention's effectiveness may differ for larger components or for additive-manufacturing techniques other than laser powder bed fusion.
Scan strategy and printing thermal history may influence the outcome of preheating.

Failure to obtain statistically significant reductions in residual stress and improvements in mechanical properties, or observation of deleterious changes such as abnormal grain growth, is defined as falsifying the hypothesis.
